newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutz shares surge on newsletter report.
newsitem.headline: Deutz shares surge on newsletter report.

text.p: Shares in German engineering group Deutz AG jumped almost 42 percent in pre-bourse trade on Friday after a newsletter reported that the company would return to profit in 1997.
The shares were quoted up 3.53 marks at 12 marks at 0845 GMT. At the same time the IBIS DAX index of 30 leading shares was down 0.2 percent or 6.67 points at 3,389.07.

The Platow Brief newsletter reported that Deutz, formerly called Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG and rescued in a one billion-mark bail-out last year, would forecast a profit at its annual results conference on May 15.
The newsletter also said the company would concentrate further on its core business by selling stakes in the coming months.
Deutz has said it hopes to break even in 1996 after making a group net loss of 1.13 billion marks in 1995 due to losses on Saudi cement plant contracts.
The company now plans to concentrate on its diesel engine business.
Deutsche Bank AG is Deutz's largest shareholder with a 48 percent stake and is also its largest creditor.
